newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold firms, silver easier.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold firms, silver easier.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 35 rupees higher at 4,825 rupees per 10 grammes vs previous close of 4,790. Renewed seasonal buying and restricted inflow evident. Gold was down by 15 rupees per 10 gramme on Saturday.

** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 400 rupees higher at 56,400 rupees per piece against previous close of 56,000. They were down by 200 rupees per piece on Saturday and by 2,200 during last week.

** Silver (.999) closed 100 rupees lower at 7,375 rupees per kg against previous closing of 7,475 rupees on the back of increased arrivals of the imported silver while industrial buyers kept sidelines in the falling market. Silver was down by 25 rupees per kg on Saturday.

Fresh physical buying ahead of the summer wedding season, which starts at the end of this month, and some shortage of supplies helped 24 carat gold close 35 rupees higher at 4,825 rupees per 10 gramme against previous closing of 4,790.
Gold was down by 15 rupees per 10 gramme on Saturday and by 185 rupees during last week.

Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 400 rupees higher at 56,400 rupees against previous closing of 56,000 rupees per piece. They were down by 200 rupees on Saturday and by 2,200 rupees during last week.

Silver (.999) closed 100 rupees lower at 7,375 rupees per kg against previous closing of 7,475 rupees on the back of increased arrivals of imported silver while industrial buyers kept sidelines expecting further declines.
Silver was down by 25 rupees per kg on Saturday and by 170 rupees during last week.
"The Delhi bullion market is witnessing higher arrivals of imported silver and traders from the Delhi remained active sellers in the Bombay market today," brokers added. (Conversion $1=35.85 rupees)
